# Astronomical 0.2.69
This release makes multi-turn conversations faster and improves first-request latency after a model load.
## Faster multi-turn conversations
Continuing a conversation no longer re-reads the previous turn's attention state from the on-disk prompt cache. The engine now retains the completed generation's state in memory — bounded by a retention policy tied to the memory ceiling — and adopts it directly on the next turn of the same conversation. The retained state is byte-identical to what the disk restore produced, so responses are unchanged; the eliminated re-read cost grows with conversation length and is largest when the disk cache is cold. Enabled by default for the resident and K2 Horizon MoVA serving families, with a status-surface diagnostic that reports whether each turn was served from memory or from disk.
## Faster first request after model load
The K2 Horizon MoVA serving family now warms its forward path once at load — compiling the decode path and touching the hot buffers — so the measured one-time warm-up cost moves from your first prompt into the load step.
## Optional per-stage prompt attribution
A new opt-in configuration flag splits prompt-processing time by stage (attention versus other compute) on supported families, and the status surface now reports richer prompt-cache diagnostics, making slow prompts attributable to specific stages.
## Clarity renames
The background service package is now `astronomical-daemon`, and the command-line app is `astronomical-cli`. Configuration files, on-disk state, and daily workflows are unaffected.
## Compatibility
- No breaking configuration changes; existing configuration loads as before. - Conversations, model caches, and on-disk state are preserved across the update. - Distributed as a signed and notarized DMG for Apple silicon (macOS 14.0 and above) with a signed Sparkle update feed; the published artifacts are digest-verified against the reviewed release manifest.
